source: Although I must admit myself a jealous man, I cannot keep Hamlet all to myself.
Because you love him.
That I do. And despite my best efforts, I don't believe I shall ever stop.
'All to myself?'
You're a little slow on the uptake, aren't you?
My lady, your husband has been concealing some information about your sister. She's passed away.
Yes. Margaret.
Margaret is...
Margaret is dead?
The King felt it best to keep this information private from you. Because of everything you've been through lately.
But I didn't feel it was right to hide this.
Your husband received a letter describing the situation. It was addressed from her nephew. Charles.
Oh, my God in Heaven. Margaret is dead. I can hardly believe it. It doesn't feel true.
But if it is true...
Why would he hide this from me?
Does he think me so weak that I cannot stand to hear about the well-being of my own family?
Ah. What am I saying? It doesn't matter.
She's dead. Margaret is dead. It sounds strange on my lips.
One believes there is always time, Ophelia. That's the problem. I thought there'd be time to see her again.
And then...
My sister was the only one in the whole world who ever understood me.
My son, my husbands, my closest friends. None of them knew me as she did.
And now the only person who truly grasped the inner workings of my heart is dead.
I-- I feel exhausted.
My lady, you're going through so many things right now. Sleep if you must.
Yes. Sleep. I must sleep.
It feels so strange. I spent the last six years trying to find a way to see Margaret.
Yet now no manner of travel can ever bring me to her. No letter I write can ever reach her.
Thank you for letting me know, Ophelia. But I need to be alone now.
I understand, my lady.
You know as I do that Gertrude's sister is dead, and you've kept the news from her. Why?
What? How on earth did you learn of it?
Heard a rumor in town. Word travels fast, I suppose.
Bloody hell. It'll be just a moment before my wife learns of it, then.
I wanted to shield her, Ophelia. I wanted to save her the pain. She's not in her right mind.
If I could keep her from suffering just a little longer... she might be strong enough to bear the news.
Or so I thought. Please don't tell her.
I've learned that the Queen's sister has passed away. Margaret. Did you know her?
What a great woman she was. How horrid.
She lived a full life. Like me, she bore no children.
I suspect she always envied Gerta on some level for that.
Gerta will be devastated when she finds out.
No. I didn't. As far as I know, she's never visited Denmark.
Still, Gertrude talks about her a lot. And she doesn't seem to be in the... best of states.
I worry about what Gertrude will do when she hears of the death.
Your aunt has passed. Margaret. Your mother's sister.
My mother's sister? Ah, yes. I vaguely recall the one. I've never met her.
Well, that's a pity. But it can't be helped.
Can you tell me anything about your history with Horatio?
Well, history makes it sound so dry.
Would you believe there was a time when we weren't friends? In the beginning, I didn't care for him much at all.
My father had asked him to dog me, you see, and report on my comings and goings.
I called him 'Nursemaid' for several months. I do not believe he enjoyed the title.
I could have, I think. But we had a rather distressing conversation, and now I'm questioning it all.
Horatio has been one of the most impactful people in my life. I shall leave it at that.
What's your history with Hamlet?
In what regard?
You two have known each other for quite some time, haven't you?
Yes. We certainly have.
I think the full description of our friendship would be at best saccharine, and at worst boring.
But you know, the moment I began to like Hamlet was the night we first discussed you.
We had come from hearing one of the great writers of the area lecture on his work. Afterwards, we went for a drink.
I remember feeling Hamlet was unusually well equipped to discuss literature for a surly teenage boy.
When I pressed him on where he had developed such a liking, he mentioned you'd given many of the great works to him to read.
I thought, goodness, this Ophelia woman sounds like quite the scholar!
And yet I feel as if my time at Hamlet's side is soon to come to a close.
He will always be one of my closest friends. But maybe some distance from him would do us both good.
My lady, what do you know of Hamlet and Horatio's friendship?
Quite a lot! My husband was rather fond of Horatio when Horatio served as a soldier, and he first introduced the two boys.
I never got to know Horatio properly until he came here to Elsinore recently. It's rather a shame.
But, you know, before they went to Wittenberg, the two of them didn't get along very well at all. It's wonderful to see things have changed.
After all, my son has often had a number of hangers-on, but very few true friends of the heart.
You went to school with them both. Can you tell me anything about Hamlet and Horatio's history?
I could write volumes. What in particular are you concerned with?
I believe I can trust you with this: I suspect there may have been something more to their relationship than friendship.
And I also suspect he might be struggling with it alone.
Oh. That.
Yes. There is certainly something like that, isn't there?
I think this is something Horatio won't admit to on his own.
Has anyone spoken to him about it in further detail?
But I might be the one best able to do so. I think I understand what's happening here.
I'll see if I can find Horatio and have a word with him.
I spoke to Horatio earlier about this very thing. I hope what I had to say was helpful.
Whatever he chooses to do next, we have to support him as best as we can.
Oh, yes! So many things. Why? What?
I believe I can trust you with this: I suspect there may be something more to their relationship than friendship.
I'm not sure whether they ever spoke of it.
And Hamlet's gone now, and, well--
You know, Rosie should go have a chat with Horatio about it. She always knows just what to say.
I'd just put my foot in my mouth! I'm certain!
I'll tell Rosencrantz to find Horatio. Then she'll have to tell me if she hears anything really juicy.
Rosey went off to talk to Horatio earlier. She gives far better advice than I ever could.
Does everyone not know that already?
Well, I'm not certain Hamlet does.
I suppose the ones who need to know have been informed now.
What do you know of Horatio's history with Prince Hamlet?
Not much. Merely that Hamlet went away to Wittenberg with Horatio, and when the both of them returned, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were in tow.
I believe it would be better to ask one of the latter two ladies. I have little context on the matter.
Let's just say that when you tend the bar, you hear things.
Horatio's made mention of a thing or two which gave me pause. There are feelings there he hasn't surfaced.
I think I might be able to help him with that.
Oh? The poor man's had quite a rough life. It might do him some good to have a friend step in on his behalf.
